intro: Wet room installation in Borthwickway typically costs between £6,000 and £12,000, depending on the size of the space, the complexity of the waterproofing required, and the quality of fixtures you choose. For a small village in Midlothian, that might sound like a significant investment — and it is — but a properly installed wet room adds real value to your home and can last decades with minimal upkeep. Whether you're adapting a bathroom for accessibility or simply wanting a sleek, modern shower space, getting the groundwork right from the start is what separates a wet room that performs well from one that causes damp problems further down the line.
localContext: Borthwickway presents some genuinely interesting challenges for wet room installations, and understanding the local property stock matters a lot here. Older stone-built properties and period cottages — which make up a good proportion of homes in and around Borthwickway — often have solid floors, uneven subfloor levels, and original joinery that needs careful consideration before any tanking or drainage work begins. The walls in these older buildings can also hold more moisture than modern construction, which means the waterproofing membrane needs to be applied meticulously and given proper curing time. Modern estate homes in Borthwickway are generally more straightforward, with timber joists and standard plasterboard that respond predictably to the tanking process. It's also worth knowing that Borthwickway sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale buildup on shower screens, fixtures, and drainage channels is a genuine consideration. Choosing fittings with descaler-friendly finishes and fitting a water softener or inline filter can save you a lot of cleaning effort over the years.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Borthwickway follows a clear sequence of work, though the specifics vary depending on your property. The process starts with a thorough survey — a good installer will check your floor structure, assess the existing plumbing layout, and confirm the drain position before any tools come out. In older Borthwickway properties, this survey stage is especially important because solid stone floors may require specialist cutting equipment and extra waterproofing layers compared to a suspended timber floor. Once the survey is complete and a design is agreed, the existing bathroom fittings are stripped out. The subfloor is then prepared — levelled if necessary — and a linear or central drain is set into the floor at the correct fall gradient to ensure water drains away efficiently rather than pooling. Tanking comes next, which involves applying a waterproof membrane across all floor and wall surfaces. This is the most critical part of the job; any gaps or poorly bonded sections will eventually allow water ingress, so this stage should never be rushed. Once the tanking has cured, wall and floor tiles are fitted, the shower system is plumbed in, and all fixtures — screens, valves, and accessories — are installed and sealed. A final check of the drainage and water pressure confirms everything is working correctly before the space is handed over.
pricing: In Borthwickway, most wet room installations fall somewhere between £6,000 and £12,000 for a standard family bathroom conversion. A straightforward installation in a modern estate home — with a suspended timber floor and easy access to existing plumbing — will sit toward the lower end of that range. Older stone-built properties and period cottages often push costs higher due to the additional preparation work involved with solid floors and older pipework. The choice of tiles, shower valve, and fixtures also has a significant impact; mid-range materials are typically included in estimates around £7,000–£9,000, while premium finishes and underfloor heating can take the total closer to £12,000 or beyond. Always request a detailed, itemised quote.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickway and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely makes a difference on a job like this. Local installers will have worked in the same types of stone-built properties and period cottages that are common here, so they're not learning on your job how to deal with solid floors or older drainage layouts. They'll also have reliable relationships with local suppliers, which matters when you're waiting on specific tiles or a replacement part mid-installation. And practically speaking, if something needs a follow-up visit after the work is complete, a local tradesperson in Borthwickway is far easier to get back quickly than someone who travelled from further afield.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built property in Borthwickway?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — though it requires more preparation than a modern home. Solid stone floors need specialist cutting for the drain channel, and the tanking process needs to account for the naturally higher moisture content in older walls. An experienced installer who understands Borthwickway's period properties will plan for this from the survey stage rather than encountering surprises mid-job.

faqs.q: Will limescale be a problem with a wet room in Borthwickway?
faqs.a: Borthwickway is in a moderately hard water area, so yes, limescale can build up on shower screens, tiles, and drainage channels over time. It's worth discussing this with your installer before work begins — they may recommend an inline water filter, a matt tile finish that shows less buildup, or fittings designed to be easy to descale. It's a manageable issue with the right choices upfront.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Borthwickway?
faqs.a: For most homes in Borthwickway, a wet room installation takes between five and ten working days from strip-out to completion. Older properties with solid floors or more complex plumbing layouts may take a day or two longer. The tanking membrane also needs adequate curing time before tiling can begin, so trying to rush this stage is something a good installer won't do regardless of schedule pressure.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a wet room in Borthwickway?
faqs.a: In most cases, no — wet room installations are considered internal alterations and don't require planning permission in Borthwickway. However, if your home is a listed building, which applies to some of the older stone properties in Midlothian, you'll need to check with the local planning authority before any structural or drainage alterations are made. Your installer should flag this during the survey if it's relevant.
